## What this case checks

Provide a canonical multipoint encoded as KML so format-specific loader behavior can be compared directly against the GeoJSON baseline.

## Risk types covered

- [`format_comparison`](../risk/format-comparison.md)

## Notes

### Purpose
Tests MultiPoint geometry loading from KML format.

### Data
- Geometry: `MULTIPOINT ((10 50), (10.2 50.1), (10.4 50.2))`
- Attributes: `id` = 1, `name` = `multipoint_kml_baseline`
- The KML driver reads `name` back as `Name` and synthesizes
  `description`, `timestamp`, `begin`, `end`, `altitudeMode`,
  `tessellate`, `extrude`, `visibility`, `drawOrder` and `icon`
  regardless of file content.
- Feature count: 1

### Validation
- Geometry type: `MultiPoint`
- CRS: `EPSG:4326`
- Geometry equals `simple_valid_multipoint` under `shapely.normalize`, which is how
  `tests/unit/test_cross_format_canonical.py` compares them. The comparison is
  winding-insensitive by necessity: the Shapefile specification mandates the
  opposite ring orientation from RFC 7946, and OGR rewrites winding on write.
  Orientation itself is asserted by `shapefile_ring_orientation`.

### Generation
Generated by `scripts/generate_vector_fixtures.py` — do not hand-edit. The
geometry is derived from `params.canonical_source_case_id`
(`simple_valid_multipoint`), and `generate_vector_fixtures.py --check` fails on any drift.
